sections.title: el, la, un, una
sections.content: Every Spanish noun is either masculine or feminine, and the little word in front of it says which. 'El' and 'la' both mean 'the'; 'un' and 'una' both mean 'a'. In the plural they become 'los' and 'las', 'unos' and 'unas'. Masculine nouns usually end in -o and feminine ones in -a, but not always, so it is worth learning each new noun together with its article.

sections.title: a, an, some — un, una, unos, unas

items.spanish: Las hermanas de Meg son gemelas.
La profesora de español se llama Daniela.
items.english: The Spanish teacher is called Daniela.
Carlos is talking with some friends.

sections.content: 'El idioma' is masculine even though it ends in -a — a handful of words ending in -ma are. And a mixed group takes the masculine plural: three women and one man are 'los amigos'.
